- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.3) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for next period.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3) or volatile, model often over-optimistic; reduce forecast by 1–4% to align with mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above prior peak for next 3–5 days.
- If model shows steady upward trend with no recent volatility, but true outcome shows sudden drop, reduce forecast slope by 20–50% for next 5 days.
- When sentiment history shows repeated positive sentiment (e.g., 3+ consecutive >0.5), model tends to over-forecast; apply downward bias of 2–5% for next 7 days.
- If model forecast is flat or slightly rising while true outcome shows strong upward momentum, check sentiment for bullish signals; if present, increase forecast by 1–3% per day.
- If model forecast is consistently below true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, consider mean reversion bias; adjust forecast upward by 1–4% for next 5 days.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.0–0.3), model often fails to capture volatility; increase forecast variance by 1–2% to account for uncertainty.
